body.statement:
For the global average treatment effect under arbitrary neighborhood interference and separate empirical second-moment bounds on its two endpoint arms, if \(G_n\) is uniformly random among simple labeled \(d\)-regular graphs and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), then there is a universal constant \(c_0>0\) such that
\[
\Pr_{G_n}\!\left\{R_2(G)\ge c_0\frac d n\right\}\longrightarrow1.
\]

source.locator: Corollary 5.4 and Appendix E.4 (random regular graphs), arXiv:2608.04909
source.verbatim_statement: Suppose $G$ is a random $d$-regular graph with $d=o(\sqrt n)$. Then, with probability at least $1-o(1)$ over the random choice of $G$, $\frac d n\lesssim \mathcal R(G,\tau_{\mathrm{GATE}},2)\lesssim \frac{d^2}{n}$.

attestation.note: Primary-source attestation from arXiv TeX source downloaded via https://export.arxiv.org/e-print/2608.04909 on 2026-09-11; tex/comparisons.tex Corollary 5.4 and tex/supp_random_regular_graphs.tex Appendix E.4 proof.

body.justification: This is the matching primary-source lower bound that remains after the unsupported stronger balanced-hole switching claim is removed.
body.gap: The cited corollary proves the \(d/n\) lower edge for random-regular GATE; it does not prove the stronger \((d+1)^2/[n\log(d+2)]\) edge.
body.consumer: The repaired all-procedure lower theorem combines this growing-degree edge with the deterministic \(1/n\) branch.
